body: Hi, please make the benchmarks easier to digest. Ideally, i'd like to see graphs (but I'm open to make them for you if you don't know how). And please add some interpretation about them, too. Where do you see improvements? Where do you see regressions? Where do you see risks? And how do you assess the change overall, regarding why it is needed?

> Hi, please make the benchmarks easier to digest. Ideally, i'd like to see graphs (but I'm open to make them for you if you don't know how). And please add some interpretation about them, too. Where do you see improvements? Where do you see regressions? Where do you see risks? And how do you assess the change overall, regarding why it is needed?

I added the relevant benchmarks to the PR itself instead of linking to seperate threads. I also added my specs, my interpretation of the results, and the differences between HashSet and AHashSet.

Some more comments at the current state:

First off, you don't mention any risks of this type in comparison to `HashSet` in the PR description. Remember that `HashMap` [has some pointer stability affordances](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/architecture/core_types.html) that `AHashMap` does not have, which always makes it a bit risky to exchange uses of `HashMap` with `AHashMap`. Does this trade-off apply to `HashSet` vs `AHashSet` as well?
If there are truly no risks, it would be appropriate to replace `HashSet` instead of introducing a new `AHashSet`.

No matter if you're replacing `HashSet` or adding `AHashSet`, its interface should copy `HashSet`'s exactly. Please don't add any new public methods to it if it can be avoided.

Since you're effectively re-implementing `AHashMap`, we need to see benchmarks of the old vs new implementation here as well. Hot benchmarks should suffice, if you didn't change any indirections. The last time I tried abstracting over the hash table implementation, I got some performance regressions, so I am careful with refactors around `AHashMap`.

Finally, your implementation is a bit larger than current `master` (regarding `AHashMap`, `RawAHashTable` + `AHashSet`, vs `AHashMap` + `HashSet`). I would normally expect logic consolidations to be less complex / smaller than separate implementations. It might be worth it to double check the implementation with this in mind (with the caveat that I haven't looked at the code much myself yet).

`HashSet` at least doesn't offer insertion order, not sure about general pointer stability, from the note in the header of that type it seems to not offer pointer stability either on adding/removing elements

HashSet does not have any pointer stability guaranties. The comment docs even suggest the use of RBSet for pointer stability.

> If there are truly no risks, it would be appropriate to replace HashSet instead of introducing a new AHashSet.

Because it would bloat the PR and making the review even harder, I replaced only one instance. I believe replacement of other HashSet instances would suit better for a seperate PR. In the PR, I linked to a branch that does exactly that to show that it is possible.

> No matter if you're replacing HashSet or adding AHashSet, its interface should copy HashSet's exactly. Please don't add any new public methods to it if it can be avoided.

I did copy AHashMap's API while remaining compatible with HashSet. If I remove the new APIs, then it would cease to be "AHashMap but is a set". I can remove some APIs from both (eg. `replace_key`, it is not used at all in the codebase).

Did a hot access bench. The one on the left is old, and the right is new. Because of how CSVs work, I kinda messed up the formatting.
[bench_map.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23541507/bench_map.csv)

There seems to be a lot of fluctiation in numbers, not sure if it is the result of the code changes or system noise. The regressions seem to be mostly correlate with erase but insert existing is generally improved, sometimes with 20% differences. I am unable to see a clear causation for this.

I haven't looked at how exactly you're measuring, but if you're experiencing fluctuations, perhaps you should run your benchmarks for longer?
Benchmarks tend to converge only in the ~1s range (per benchmark), and if I understand your results correctly, you're more in the ~0.05s range.

> I haven't looked at how exactly you're measuring, but if you're experiencing fluctuations, perhaps you should run your benchmarks for longer? Benchmarks tend to converge only in the ~1s range (per benchmark), and if I understand your results correctly, you're more in the ~0.05s range.

I used the same bench as the mentioned *basic bench*, but with no cache flush and `run_len` is 2_000_000. I now tested with `run_len` of 20_000_000.
[bench_map.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23566893/bench_map.csv)

The regression seems less severe now but is still there. I am not sure why it is there or why it is only consistently there for `erase` but not others.
Removing `a_hash_map.cpp‎` seems to fix to the MSVC issue, and AHashMap was the only Map/Set implementation with a `.cpp` file as well. I don't think the removal of it changes much.
